title: Bringing Real Harnesses and User Feedback Back into Training
subtitle: Harness adapters · Online RL · A classic in empirical scaling
intro: Two new technical posts examine training–deployment consistency: LoRA training inside native agent harnesses and continuous updates from single live conversational rollouts. A brief covers variable-loop architecture; the classic revisits how empirical learning curves are measured. Another brief covers a layered-architecture view of embodied post-training.
window: November 18–21, 2026 (Philadelphia time; emphasis on updates since the previous issue, including delayed indexing)

blocks.text: A proxy records exact tokens from Qwen3.8-27B running native Pi, Hermes and OpenCode loops; asynchronous GRPO trains a LoRA for each. Tasks first undergo reference, no-op, wrong-solution and replay checks, then retain cases the base model sometimes solves. [1]

blocks.text: The three final runs total 598 steps, 78,114 samples and 167M trained tokens. Each adapter uses 2×B200, one for sampling and one for training, with thinking off during rollouts. The table reports within-harness pass@1 on SWE-bench Pro hard-51, one attempt per task, capped at 2 hours, 100 agent steps and 131,072 tokens. [1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Tool-call reductions condition on tasks solved by both models and cannot be converted into overall training speedups. Merge weights were selected on Terminal-Bench, introducing selection optimism; AutomationBench transfer shows no clear general improvement. [1]

blocks.text: A user experiences one reply, preventing a group of human rollouts from the same state. Kaon archives exact tokens, actual sampling probabilities q, the top-k head and weight versions, bounds policy-version lag, then updates LoRA. Truncated trajectories receive no appended EOS. [2]

blocks.label: TIS controls large ratios; Score Centering corrects mismatch-induced drift. This is a clipped, top-k approximation with no unbiasedness guarantee supplied.

blocks.text: Length ablations find that averaging within replies before averaging across replies interacts with advantage imbalance to favor short replies. Global-token aggregation or revised balancing stabilizes length but removes roughly half the early apparent turn gain. Combining both fixes performs worse because their aggregation units differ. [2]

blocks.text: The exact reward, absolute sample sizes and absolute metrics are undisclosed. Session depth is behavioral and does not directly measure welfare or correctness. The early +14.7% includes length bias and is not a corrected net gain. [2]

blocks.text: The middle 12 of 24 physical layers repeat three times, giving 6+3×12+6=48 layer visits. articles.paper: The Death of System 1: Why VLA and WAM Imitation Learning Is Fading
articles.title: Embodied post-training: a layered-architecture argument
articles.evidence: Read the text; a synthesis, not a new controlled experiment

blocks.text: The author combines simulation RL post-training of reasoning models with low-level contact-control RL to argue that intermediate imitation policies may become optional tools. A concrete interface is high-level target poses/skills with low-level fast feedback. The proposed disappearance of the imitation layer is the author’s conjecture; existing task results do not establish universal replacement across robots, latency constraints and distribution shifts. [6]

classic.question: With a fixed data pool and increasing reuse, how would an experiment distinguish a changed power-law exponent from saturation of the effective independent sample count?

blocks.text: Before Kaplan (2020) and Chinchilla (2022), Hestness et al. (2017) measured data learning curves across translation, language, images and speech. The object is validation error after model selection, not loss versus steps along one training run. [4]

blocks.tex: |T_i|=m_i\approx 2^i m_0,\qquad V\cap T_i=\varnothing,\qquad \widehat M_i\in\arg\min_{M\in\mathcal M_i}L(M\mid T_i,V)
blocks.label: Mathematical restatement of the protocol: randomly shuffle, roughly double shard sizes, search capacity and optimization settings, and use a fixed validation set. This defines a composite learning curve.
Empirical fits from the paper: error curves may include offset γ; required model size s(m) grows sublinearly in several experiments.

blocks.text: Composite-curve exponents from Appendix A Table 1 follow. Metrics differ, so these are not directly comparable gains in a common quality measure. [4]

blocks.label: My algebraic rearrangement: converting target error into data and model multipliers requires remaining in the same power-law regime with a fixed floor γ.
My interpretation: a lower intercept and a changed slope are different evidence. A finite-range line does not automatically extrapolate to a new data distribution.

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The observation that architectures/optimizers often shift intercepts is limited to the tested tasks and search; it is not an exponent-invariance theorem. Using V for selection and error measurement is not an independent-test guarantee. [4]
